name: Glassback drake

baseline.name: Glassback drake
baseline.look: Low six-limbed lizard with overlapping translucent back plates.
baseline.ecology: Nests beneath stable glass crust and eats salt beetles.
baseline.limit: Senses ground vibration; dazzling plates reflect light but do not fire beams.
baseline.encounter: Move on bedrock, avoid nest bowls and wait out a threat display.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: At cool dawn a drake noses salt beetles from cracks. It warms against stable glass crust, then rests under the rim. Its plates change apparent color with the light rather than changing physical shape.
cycle: Nests occupy bowls beneath old fused crust. Hatchlings use shallow cracks and depend on the same beetle habitat. New windblown glass can hide a nest without moving it.
signs: Parallel six-foot tracks terminate at crust edges. A raised plate fan and a still body warn more clearly than a spectacular reflected flash.
escalation: Freeze -> plate fan -> sideways blocking step -> short bite or shove if crowded. A quiet withdrawal gives it space; vibration tricks are unreliable and may draw it closer.
community: Ossara caravan crews retain bedrock approaches even when a dune shortcut looks faster. Nest closures protect animals and prevent expensive broken loads.
scene: A reflected flash seems to place a suspect at an observatory. Maela finds that a drake plate redirected the light: an image proves light arrived, not how the whole event occurred.
motion: Six limbs stay in three consistent pairs. Lock the plate count and major overlaps for a shot; animate a fan as hinged groups, not melting shards.
sounds: Claws on glass, dry plate clicks and a short hiss. No beams or magical signal reception.
rule: Low six-limbed lizard, translucent overlapping plates; no wings, fire breath or projected energy.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
